reason: I want to follow filtering first; the picture shows small substances passing through gaps while larger blood components stay behind.
expectation: I expect the filter to separate water and other small substances from blood cells and large proteins, though some useful substances may pass through too.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would build the urine route, but I want to see filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose, salts and water through along with wastes, so recovery is the next part to follow.
reaction: It was interesting that filtering doesn't just separate out waste.
reason: The recovery tube's picture shows useful substances returning to blood, which follows naturally from filtering.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to blood, leaving fluid containing waste.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to follow recovery first.

effect: Useful substances and much water return to blood, while waste-containing fluid continues down the tube. I can now build the urinary route.
reaction: It makes sense why the recovery step matters after the filter let useful substances through.
reason: The ureters connect the kidneys toward the bladder, so they seem like the next part of the route.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidney outlets, leaving a connection toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also belongs to the urinary system, but the ureters come between it and the kidneys.

effect: The ureters are attached to the kidneys, leaving the bladder to complete the drainage route.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the bladder connects to the ureters.
expectation: I expect the bladder to attach as a storage sac for fluid draining from the kidneys.

effect: The kidneys, ureters and bladder now form a route where urine can collect.
reaction: The route from kidneys to bladder is clear.
reason: I want to follow the recovered kidney fluid into the completed drainage route.
expectation: I expect the remaining waste-containing fluid to become urine and travel toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the organs to the body also meets a goal, but I want to finish following the fluid first.

effect: The remaining fluid follows the urinary route to the bladder while blood continues separately; the filtering goal is complete.
reaction: It was useful to see the urine and blood routes kept separate.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it connects the urinary organs to the body.
expectation: I expect the kidneys, ureters and bladder to join the body model and complete the remaining goal.

effect: The urinary organs are connected to the body and its blood circulation, completing the chapter.
reaction: The final picture makes the blood supply and route out of the body clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile. It showed why the kidney needs more than a filter that removes waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder was straightforward but less interesting than following the fluid.

surprise.text: I was surprised that useful glucose and water pass through the filter along with wastes and have to be recovered.

arbitrary.text: None felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained the parts' purposes.

continue.text: I would probably continue: following the filter and recovery route made me curious about how other body processes work.
